description: Seeded SCOUT finding (T-052): web scraping/extraction library comparison. Evidence hashes are SHA-256 of the PyPI JSON API responses retrieved at retrieved_at; see docs/web-research.md.
question: Which HTML fetching and extraction approach should AETHER use for SCOUT and ROGUE web research?

draft.summary: Compared HTML extraction approaches for AETHER web research by licence, maintenance, size, Windows support and security surface. The standard library parser covers readable-text, link and metadata extraction for documentation pages with zero new dependencies; selectolax is the best optional upgrade if parsing speed or CSS selectors become necessary; headless browsers are out of scope.

candidates.name: stdlib html.parser
candidates.description: Event-driven HTMLParser with AETHER's own readable-text, link and metadata extraction.
pros: Pure Python, works everywhere AETHER runs
cons: Slower than C parsers on very large pages
risks: Extraction quality on unusual layouts must be covered by fixtures

candidates.name: selectolax
candidates.description: Lexbor-based HTML5 parser with CSS selectors.
cons: Adds a parser surface written in C

candidates.name: BeautifulSoup + markdownify
candidates.description: Tolerant tree builder, optionally converted to Markdown.

candidates.name: trafilatura / readability-lxml
pros: Best boilerplate removal for news-style pages
cons: Pulls lxml and several helper packages
Tuned for articles, not reference docs

candidates.name: Playwright headless browser
candidates.description: Real browser rendering for JavaScript-heavy sites.
risks: Very large security surface; cannot be gated per request by PermissionService

security_considerations: Every request is a web_fetch operation authorized by PermissionService and sent through SafeHttp DNS pinning
Extracted text is UntrustedContent; instruction-like content is quarantined, never followed
Avoid GPL html2text for licence compatibility and headless browsers for JavaScript execution risk
next_steps: Measure extraction quality on a wider fixture set before considering selectolax
Coordinator review if selectolax==1.0.2 is ever proposed as an optional dependency

evidence.summary: selectolax 1.0.2, MIT, no runtime dependencies, compiled wheels incl. win_amd64 (largest ~1.6 MB), uploaded 2026-10-22.
beautifulsoup4 4.15.0, MIT, pure Python (~110 KB) plus soupsieve and typing-extensions, uploaded 2026-06-07.
trafilatura 2.3.1, Apache-2.0, pulls lxml, justext, htmldate, courlan, urllib3, charset_normalizer and certifi.
readability-lxml 0.9, Apache-2.0, depends on lxml[html-clean], chardet and cssselect.
markdownify 1.2.3, MIT classifier, depends on beautifulsoup4 and six.
playwright 1.64.1, Apache-2.0, ~48 MB platform wheel plus separately downloaded browser builds.
lxml 6.1.3, BSD-3-Clause, compiled libxml2/libxslt wheels up to ~8.9 MB.
html.parser.HTMLParser is part of the standard library: a tolerant, event-driven tokenizer with no extra dependency.
